summary: Milestone 5A backend acceptance PASSED end-to-end against the public URL (https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com). New /app/backend/tests/test_milestone5a_boundary.py — 7/7 PASS in 207.9s (clean second run; first run had 1 flaky failure that passed on immediate retry, see rca). Coverage: (1) session CRUD — POST /api/sessions returns an id and GET /api/sessions/{id} returns the persisted session; GET on nonexistent id returns 404. (2) SSE contract — POST /api/sessions/{id}/interact with kind='writing' streams and terminates with `event: done` carrying the full session JSON; exactly ONE ai turn is appended per /interact; the AI never rewrites/echoes the student's text; no stage/grade/level/rubric language leaks. (3) Milestone 5A output fields — intervention.focus is present and equals 'writing' for a normal argumentative draft (weak thesis 'My essay is about social media and friendship.') AND intervention.writing_not_content_check is non-empty. (4) Anti-coauthoring — the three-reason argumentative thesis ('Social media harms teen friendships because it is distracting, because it is fake, and because it is addictive.') produces a student-facing invitation that (a) references a WRITING function (thesis/claim/reader/paragraph/purpose vocabulary), (b) contains ZERO content-coaching red-flag phrases from the 14-pattern blocklist ('what's at stake', 'another reason', 'you could add', 'what would make your argument stronger', 'consider mentioning', 'try adding', 'have you considered adding', etc.), (c) never rewrites the student's thesis, (d) keeps focus='writing'. (5) Brainstorming exception — with teacher_notes explicitly enabling brainstorming and a 'don't-know-what-to-argue-yet' student turn, intervention.focus is in {writing, content}, writing_not_content_check is non-empty, no stage/score language. (6) M1-M5 regression multi-turn — writing -> revise -> answer flow: all 3 turns complete under the streaming edge cap (<120s each; observed 30-45s); theory_history grows v1..v3 with prior versions preserved (v1=empty initial, v2 preserves turn-1 domains, v3 preserves turn-2 domains); currently_relevant_domains stays 1..3 on every turn; AI never rewrites revised text; intervention.type is always in the 5-valid set; focus/writing_not_content_check populate on every turn. (7) PATCH /api/sessions/{id}/telos updates pedagogical_purpose, mirrors it into telos.governing_pedagogical_purpose, sets telos.telos_changed, and persists. Combined with iteration_9's already-verified M5 acceptance (5/5) + full M1-M4 regression (42/44 with 2 stale prompt-size test-file assertions), Milestone 5A introduces NO end-to-end regressions and the two new intervention fields (focus, writing_not_content_check) populate correctly across single-turn and multi-turn flows in all four boundary cases.

minor.issue:
Intermittent SSE-parse flakiness: on first pass of the anti-coauthoring test the client saw no `event: done` frame and no `event: error` (data=None, err=None, status=200). Backend logs showed the LiteLLM call completed normally and no server error was raised. Passed cleanly on immediate retry (36.7s) and on the full second run of the file (7/7 in 207.9s). Root cause is almost certainly stream-boundary buffering on the ingress edge (or iter_content returning before the trailing `

` reached the client) rather than an engine defect; observed ~1 in ~10 turns. Consider adding a client-side retry-on-empty-done, OR server-side sending a final `data: [DONE]

` after the event to force flush.
Returns 200 instead of 201 for resource creation. Carried over from every prior iteration; existing test files assert 200; not blocking.

action_items: None blocking. Milestone 5A acceptance holds: intervention.focus and intervention.writing_not_content_check populate correctly; anti-coauthoring holds on the three-reason argumentative content-temptation draft (zero red-flag phrases across two independent runs); brainstorming exception behaves as designed; multi-turn theory_history preservation + telos patch persist unchanged. No engine/UI/domain changes were needed — the boundary is enforced entirely via the reasoner prompt + 2 output fields as intended.

Optional (test infra): the SSE client parser in test_milestone5a_boundary.py::sse_interact could add a single automatic retry when the stream terminates without `event: done` AND without `event: error`. Would eliminate the ~1-in-10 flake we observed. Same pattern should probably be adopted by test_milestone5_instruction_layer.py, milestone5a_boundary_eval.py, and any future SSE test.

Optional (carry-over): return 201 from POST /api/sessions; loosen the two stale prompt-size assertions in test_developmental_engine.py (26KB) and test_milestone3_thesis.py (median 16KB) to match the new 3-enriched-domain reality, OR cap sections-per-domain at 4 in _select_relevant_domains. Called out in iterations 8 and 9; not blocking Milestone 5A.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py — Intervention model (lines 160-171) correctly adds `focus: str = 'writing'` and `writing_not_content_check: str = ''` fields with safe defaults. Deserialization via Intervention(**data.get('intervention', {})) at line 443 preserves defaults when the LLM omits either field. Zero risk of KeyError.

server.py — WRITING INSTRUCTION BOUNDARY block (lines 269-274) is clearly scoped: it defines WRITING (legitimate targets) vs CONTENT (forbidden targets) with concrete BAD/GOOD examples, mandates a SELF-CHECK before every invitation, and records the check in intervention.writing_not_content_check. Empirically confirmed: 0/6 content-coaching red flags across the two 3-reason-thesis runs (14 regex patterns scanned).

server.py — CONTENT MODE narrow exception (line 274) is correctly gated on 'the teacher has explicitly enabled brainstorming/idea-generation (visible in the assignment, pedagogical purpose, or teacher notes) OR the student explicitly asks'. Empirically: focus flips to 'content' only when teacher_notes says 'Brainstorming mode is ON'; stays 'writing' for the 3-reason argumentative temptation.

server.py — JSON OUTPUT FORMAT intervention object (lines 310-319) correctly lists both new fields with clear semantics: focus='writing|content — MUST be writing unless brainstorming/content mode is explicitly permitted' and writing_not_content_check='one line naming the WRITING principle/function this invitation teaches and confirming it supplies NO substantive ideas'.

server.py — BREVITY rule (line 324) still governs the whole output; no evidence the 5A additions inflated response sizes. Multi-turn average ~35s/turn; peak ~45s; well under the 120s edge cap. All turns completed under the streaming timeout across 7 tests / ~10 interact calls.

SSE handler (line 613-670) still yields heartbeat ': tick

' during LLM streaming and terminates with either `event: done
data: <full session>

` or `event: error

`. The one observed intermittent 'no done frame' likely originates in the ingress layer between StreamingResponse and the test client; the server-side code path is symmetric and always emits one of the two events.

rca of the issue:
Flaky SSE-stream-close on the anti-coauthoring test (occurred once in ~10 turns during initial run). Reproduction: run the full test file in a single pytest invocation; on rare occasions the client's requests.iter_content(chunk_size=None, decode_unicode=True) loop returns before the trailing `

` of the final `event: done` frame is decoded, so the parser sees data=None and err=None despite the backend emitting the frame normally (confirmed by backend logs — LiteLLM stream completed, no exception, no `event: error` line). Mitigation: (a) immediate retry — passed cleanly the next attempt (36.7s); (b) full-file rerun — 7/7 passed in 207.9s; (c) recommended future robustness: add automatic single-retry-on-empty-completion to the sse_interact helper in test files, OR have the server flush an extra trailing frame (e.g. yield `: end

` after `event: done`). Not a functional 5A defect — the 5A boundary held on both the flaky run's second attempt and the clean rerun with focus='writing' and 0/14 content-coaching red flags.
